headline: Target comps turn positive (+5.6%) for first time in five quarters on 4.4% traffic gain; FY sales outlook doubled to ~4%.
guidance_note: FY26 net sales growth raised to ~4% (from ~2%); GAAP/adj EPS now seen near high end of $7.50-8.50; guidance excludes any tariff refunds.
key_messages: Comparable sales +5.6% (stores +4.7%, digital +8.9%), first positive comp in five quarters, led by 4.4% traffic growth.
Gross margin 29.0% vs 28.2%; adjusted EPS $1.71 vs $1.30 a year ago, well above ~$1.46 consensus.
Non-merchandise revenue (Roundel ads, Circle 360, Target+) up close to 25%.
CFO says bigger tax refunds likely propped up Q1 spending and that boost should fade; sentiment has dipped though shoppers stayed resilient.
Q2 flagged as toughest compare of the year (Nintendo Switch 2 launch anniversary); company plans conservatively and will chase inventory.

consumer.quote: While we have momentum, we're also being cautious about the near-term operating environment, with consumers weighing multiple headwinds and tailwinds.

macro_read: A sharp turn to positive traffic at Target suggests discretionary-leaning spending firmed in spring 2026, helped by larger tax refunds that management expects to fade. Softer sentiment remains a watch item.

sources.label: SGB: Target boosts FY sales guidance
